title: The Spire of the Sundered Sea
premise: Tamsin Vane, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Vael, has survived twenty years in the Sundered Valley, a pocket of the drowned kingdom of Mereth where magic cannot enter and the old world's refugees cling to borrowed lives. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley's wards, Tamsin learns she is the last keeper of Vael's dying ember and the only one who can reopen the Door that leads out of a country erased from every map. Guided by a disgraced cartographer, a witch-hunter's runaway daughter, and a dragon-fire spirit wearing her dead brother's face, she crosses the flooded ruins of Mereth pursued by the Inquisitor who silenced her god. At the Spire of the Sundered Sea, Tamsin must choose between relighting Vael and restoring magic to the world, or letting the ember die so the valley's people can finally be free of the past. She chooses to spend the ember on the Door, walks her found family into the living world, and lets the old god—and the old country—rest at last.
about_author: Coral Halloran is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing drowned-town records along a fog-bound coast before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about stubborn people, unreliable maps, and the families we assemble from shipwreck.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She takes a mercenary contract guarding a grain caravan through the Sundered Valley, establishing the magic-dead refuge and her silent vows to Vael. A crown surveyor's lantern flickers green at the ward-stone, the first crack in the valley's invisibility. Beat: uneasy routine, the sense that safety is borrowed.

chapters.title: Ash in the Offering Bowl
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the shrine, the god-ember gutters and gives her a single word: Door. The village elders refuse to believe the wards are failing. Beat: denial and dread; Tamsin realizes her faith has become a countdown.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A herald nails up the crown's edict: all bearers of the gift to be registered or burned. Neighbors she has guarded for years begin looking at the old-timers differently. Beat: betrayal by community; the valley's neutrality dies.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She breaks into the archive of Odell Ferrance, a disgraced royal mapmaker exiled to the valley, and demands the location of the Door. He refuses—until witch-hunters burn the eastern shrine. Beat: reluctant alliance forged in fire.

chapters.title: What the Ward-Stone Kept
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. He reveals the valley is not a refuge but a prison: the wards were raised to hide Mereth's last gifted children, Tamsin among them. Beat: identity shattering; her whole life was a cage built as a kindness.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Ran From the Fire
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They rescue Sefa, the Inquisitor's daughter, caught smuggling a gifted child toward the valley. Sefa carries her father's hunt-list—with Tamsin's name at the top. Beat: compassion for the enemy; the hunt becomes personal.

chapters.title: Crossing the Drowned Mile
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The company slips through the failing ward into the flooded ruins of old Mereth, where magic seeps back like cold water and Tamsin's suppressed gift wakes painfully. Beat: wonder laced with grief for a homeland she never knew.

chapters.title: The Brother Beneath the Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A dragon-fire spirit wearing her drowned brother Brannoc's face rises from a sunken chapel and offers to guide them to the Spire. Odell warns it lies; Tamsin cannot refuse. Beat: longing versus suspicion; the past given a voice.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Flashbacks and a present ambush: her father, Inquisitor Corvan, spares a gifted child publicly while burning a village privately. Sefa understands his mercy is a performance. Beat: disillusionment; she chooses Tamsin's side for good.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In a smuggler's market on a beached whale-carcass town, they trade Odell's maps for passage. Brannoc's spirit bargains secretly, and Tamsin catches the lie in his face. Beat: found family tested by the ghost between them.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Sunken Road
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. A crown gunship corners them on a causeway; Odell sacrifices his life's work—the master map of Mereth—to buy escape, keeping only the Door's coordinates in his head. Beat: grief and resolve; the mapmaker burns his own country.

chapters.title: The Ember Speaks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Vael's ember, carried in a lantern, finally speaks in full: it was not silenced by the god's death but imprisoned by Corvan's order, and only the Spire's altar can free or end it. Beat: revelation; Tamsin learns her vows were a leash.

chapters.title: The Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Corvan's riders trap the company in a salt marsh. Sefa confronts her father face to face and he offers her pardon in exchange for Tamsin. Beat: the cost of loyalty made explicit; she refuses.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Company
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The marsh battle kills two companions; Tamsin's gift erupts uncontrolled, saving the rest but scarring her hands with ember-light she can no longer hide. Beat: survivor's guilt; power as wound.

chapters.title: The Spire of the Sundered Sea
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They reach the Spire rising from a drowned caldera, its dragon-fire hearth nearly cold. Brannoc's spirit confesses he is the ember's last fragment, wearing her grief to reach the altar. Beat: heartbreak; even her brother was a memory wearing a mask.

chapters.title: Corvan at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Corvan's POV. The Inquisitor arrives not to burn Tamsin but to bargain: he silenced Vael because the god demanded a justice the crown would not survive. He offers her the truth in exchange for the ember. Beat: the antagonist humanized; justice versus order.

chapters.title: The Trial of the Silent God
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the altar, the freed ember puts Vael's own silence on trial—revealing the god abandoned Mereth to its drowning. Tamsin must judge the being she served. Beat: climax of theme; justice outside law, rendered by the wounded.

chapters.title: What the Door Costs
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Opening the Door requires the ember entire. Tamsin chooses to spend Vael—her vows, her brother's ghost-face, her last tie to Mereth—to buy her people passage into the living world. Beat: sacrifice; love outweighing faith.

chapters.title: The Last Light Goes Out
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. As the Door opens, Corvan chooses to stay behind with the dying god rather than face the crown's reckoning, asking Sefa only to remember him kindly. Beat: bittersweet farewell; even the hunter is mourned.

chapters.title: Through, Into the Living World
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The valley's people cross: old gifted children, farmers, Odell's orphaned apprentices. Tamsin walks last, watching Mereth's ruins finally sink into true sleep. Beat: release; the found family steps out of history.

chapters.title: A Map With No Valley On It
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later, in a coastal town, Sefa draws the first new map of their route and Odell's apprentices found a school. Tamsin plants the cold lantern at a crossroads shrine with no god in it. Beat: quiet rebuilding; memory kept without worship.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On the anniversary, a child at the shrine lights the lantern from her own small gift, and it holds flame. Tamsin smiles, finally unsworn and unafraid. Beat: resolution; the future lit by hands, not gods.
